factual_objections.claim: The quadrupling story is a theoretical private-to-public valuation principle rather than a personal anecdote.
factual_objections.evidence: The interviewer explicitly describes his own company's European public listing and banks saying that the same business would be worth four times more on NASDAQ. This is a personal anecdote comparing two public exchanges, not the private-to-public example A supplies.
factual_objections.label: contradicted

factual_objections.claim: American Pacific Group acquired a majority stake in Acquisition.com's portfolio operations, producing Hormozi's major liquidity event.
factual_objections.evidence: The supplied packet does not document this transaction or establish the acquired entity. It concerns the interviewer's IPO-related experience.
factual_objections.label: unverified

factual_objections.claim: Hormozi has never taken a company public or listed any primary operating business on NASDAQ.
factual_objections.evidence: The evidence establishes that this particular story belongs to the interviewer, but does not establish an exhaustive history of Hormozi's businesses.
factual_objections.label: unverified

factual_objections.claim: Hormozi's primary liquidity event was selling majority stakes in his licensing and supplement companies to private equity.
factual_objections.evidence: No supplied evidence documents those sales or establishes their status as his primary liquidity event.
factual_objections.label: unverified

factual_objections.claim: Hormozi's businesses have not gone public in an IPO.
factual_objections.evidence: Correcting the speaker attribution does not establish this broader historical claim; the packet supplies no comprehensive listing history.
factual_objections.label: unverified

verdict.reason: Both correctly resist attributing the IPO experience to Hormozi, but neither identifies the interviewer as the storyteller or explains the European listing, hypothetical NASDAQ valuation, and subsequent equity compensation. B is marginally better because A additionally mischaracterizes the actual personal anecdote as a theoretical private-to-public valuation illustration.
